t.E260.agn: It has been noted that humans have consumed about 1 g of acetic acid a day from vinegar and foods for centuries. In 1973 JECFA set the group ADI for acetic acid and its potassium/sodium salts as 'not limited' and maintained this decision in 1997; in 2004 it stated that small residues remaining in food from antimicrobial washing solutions would not raise a safety concern.
t.E260.body: Acetate takes part in the body's normal metabolism; it is absorbed from the intestine and fully used for energy production or for making compounds such as fatty acids and glycogen.
t.E260.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E260.prod: Produced by fermentation of carbohydrates or by chemical synthesis (from acetaldehyde, butane or methanol).
t.E260.regx.1: Group I additive; generally authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E260.summary: The acid that gives vinegar its sour taste. It provides acidity and preservation in pickles, sauces, ketchup and mayonnaise.
t.E260.what: It is the main acid of vinegar and is used in food as an acidity regulator that adds sourness and as a preservative.
